algorithm: Keyword-overlap intent scoring with a fallback intent

classes.desc: Rule-based chatbot: keyword scoring picks the intent, seeded RNG picks the reply.
classes.name: Chatbot

complexity: O(i*k) per message over i intents and k keywords
data_flow_ascii:
user text -> match_intent (keyword hits) -> best intent
intent -> seeded choice of canned response -> (intent_name, reply)
scripted turns or --chat loop -> printed transcript
description_sentence: A rule-based chatbot that matches intents by keyword overlap and replies from canned responses, with scripted and interactive chat modes.
failure_note: Unmatched input falls back to the help-style fallback intent, so the bot always has something sensible to say.

label: chatbot
output_shape: Prints a scripted conversation transcript with the matched intent per turn, or runs an interactive chat loop.
pitch_sentence: I built a {topic} that understands what you are asking from keywords and answers from a configurable intent table.

qa.a: Each keyword found as a substring adds one point; the highest-scoring intent wins, and the fallback intent wins ties at zero.
Keyword matching is transparent and dependency-free; it handles the demo's small intent set without any model or training data.
It never invents replies; every response comes verbatim from the intent table, so the bot cannot hallucinate.
qa.q: Can the bot say something wrong?

resume_bullet_template: Built a {topic} in Python using keyword-based intent matching with scripted and interactive conversation modes.
run_notes: --chat enables interactive input() mode; --name sets the bot's display name.
scaling_note: Keyword scoring suits tens of intents; hundreds would want TF-IDF or embeddings instead of substring counting.
storage_note: No persistence: the intent table is compiled at startup and conversations are not saved.
tradeoff_note: Rules are predictable and debuggable but brittle on paraphrases a human would find obvious.
